youtube.title: Which ocean has the most tsunamis? World Tsunami Awareness Day 🌊
youtube.description:
Atlantic, Indian or the third one? Seven in ten recorded tsunamis start in a single ocean, along one ring of earthquakes and volcanoes, yet the deadliest wave in history came from somewhere else.
Guess before the map draws it, then see the ring, the 2004 wave, the country hit most often, and the one rule that saves lives.
Which ocean did you pick?

v04.text: The Pacific. About 7 in 10 tsunamis on record start there, along the ring of quakes around its rim.

v05.text: The deadliest, though, came from the Indian Ocean in 2004, and killed around 230,000 people.

v06.text: Japan is hit more often than anywhere; its own word, harbour wave, is what the world uses.

v07.text: The 5th of November is World Tsunami Awareness Day. The lesson: feel a long quake, head for high ground.

research.topic: Ocean with the most tsunamis: the Pacific — roughly 70 % of recorded tsunamis (NOAA NCEI/WDS Global Historical Tsunami Database; ITIC), generated along the Pacific Ring of Fire subduction zones; the deadliest tsunami on record was the 26 December 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami (~230,000 deaths, 14 countries); Japan records the most tsunamis of any country and gave the world the word (tsu = harbour, nami = wave); World Tsunami Awareness Day, 5 November, designated by the UN General Assembly in 2015

myths.myth: Tsunamis are an Indian Ocean problem because of 2004.
myths.reality: About 7 in 10 recorded tsunamis occur in the Pacific; the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami was the deadliest, not the typical one.

landscape.our_gap: Tsunami Shorts are disaster footage; nobody asks the ocean question, draws the ring as the reveal, counts 2004, names the country hit most often and ends on the survival rule.
